summary: ```markdown # Half-Skirt Production Tutorial: Pleated Skirt ## Introduction Let's learn how to make a pleated skirt. In this tutorial, we will build upon the bag skirt made in the previous video. ## Removing the Gap First of all, if you want to make a pleated skirt, you have to remove the gap on the back piece. Because in the end, we will form a lot of folds in the vertical direction, it is difficult to adjust the gap. Here, we select this point and delete it, along with all the extra points. ## Preparing for Simulation After deleting, we can't simulate it directly because we need to delete the pleated line that was saved before and the pleated line of the waist. Now that our version has been modified, we will re-create the pleated line. I will use the free pleating tool for this. ### Sewing the Front and Back Pieces First, sew the front here. Then, when sewing the back piece, we should pay attention because this is the back piece. Since we just saved it and it was dug out, we will almost remove about 30mm from here. The side will be pulled up later, so our side curve is a little bit wrong, but that doesn't matter. Next, use the free pleating tool to sew the back piece to the belt. After sewing, return the belt and simulate it together. The simulation helps to make them more flat. ## Adjusting the Pleated Line After adjusting the position of the pleated line, we can re-roll the belt because we won't change it later. In addition, before we make the pleated line, we need to turn the panel into a longer panel first. ### Lengthening the Panel After selecting these two panels, drag the selection box to lengthen them. During the lengthening process, right-click can be entered to enter the specific percentage. Once we open the simulation, it becomes a long pleated skirt. ## Editing the Fabric Properties Next, we can use the edit panel tool to select these lines on the side and then open their elasticity. After opening the elasticity, this edge will shrink. We set its ratio to 60 because it was pulled up 150% before. Now, by shrinking it by 60%, it will return to the same length as before. ### Final Adjustments Turn the panel manually. After turning it on, we first reduce the particle diameter and the conflict thickness. Once we open the simulation, you will see that there are many pleats. After lowering, the next step is to adjust the fabric properties. If you think the pleats are not obvious enough, you can increase its finelining strength and the strength of the foot line. These values should be adjusted to a certain degree. If the foot line is too high, the fabric will not stretch easily, making the pleats more obvious. ## Softening the Pleats After adjusting, we open the simulation again. You will find that there are many obvious pleats. Another way to make the pleats look more pronounced is to reduce the bend strength. By reducing the bend strength in three directions, the whole pleat property will become softer, making the pleats look thinner and more obvious. I choose to reduce the bend strength because I think these pleats are already okay, but they are not smooth enough. So, we have to continue to reduce the particle diameter, which I have reduced to 8. If we want to make the pleats denser, we can reduce the elasticity on the side a little more, setting the elasticity ratio to 50. ## Combining the Skirt Parts Finally, because the whole skirt is one piece, let's combine the front and back. After making the front and back, activate the belt and simulate. If you directly activate the simulation, you will find that because there is elasticity on the side, it will shrink to the middle, causing the belt to be pulled up. ### Applying Fabric to the Belt Here, we need to copy a fabric and use it on the belt. Click on the browse option next to it, and we find "Trim Fusible Rigid." This fabric is not easy to stretch, so it won't be affected by elasticity. After using this fabric, it may not be very sweet, so we can adjust the belt to be a little narrower. ## Final Adjustments to Pleats If conditions allow, we can reduce the strength of the pleats to 5 or 3 to make them smoother. ## Moving to the Slant Pleats Skirt After learning how to make a pleated skirt, we will try a more difficult one: the slant pleats skirt. First, open the previously saved pleated skirt and merge the front and the middle. After merging, select this open line and delete it, then delete the remaining points. ### Preparing the Slant Pleats After deleting, select the front and cut a layer to the outside. After cutting out, cancel the connection. Now we have two pleats together, but we need to delete the whole circle of the lining that automatically forms the outer circle. After deleting, we first need to determine the shape of the entire skirt. Since we only have slanted pleats on the side, we will use the lining tool to sew them together at the top. After sewing, pay attention to change its lining type to "TURN" because they are in and out layers. ## Sewing the Left and Right Sides Next, use the free lining to sew the left side together. After sewing, change their lining type to "TURN" because they are still stacked together. After fixing the left side, we can do the right side first. ### Adjusting the Outer Layer First, select the outer layer of this line and the small section of the inner side. After sewing, we can freeze the inner layers that cannot be used. After freezing, select the outer layer and press SHIFT + Q to check if it is all frozen. Open the simulation to see the effect. ## Final Checks and Adjustments Press SHIFT + W to display all the boards. If we see that the side is twisted, press CTRL + C to return to the previous state. Check the error of the seam allowance. The entire back piece is sewn together with the inner layer, while the outer layer is only a small section sewn together with the inner layer. We need to consider whether the left side of the inner board should not be sewn together with the back but with the outer layer. Therefore, we have to delete the seam allowance between the inner board and the back. After deleting, simulate again. ### Ensuring Even Distribution After opening the simulation, we will see that if both boards are to remain the same, we should sew the sides of the outer board to the back pieces together. After sewing, we can hide the outer board to check if we achieve the desired effect. If we feel that the position of the seam allowance is not tight enough, we can adjust it by pulling this short seam allowance up a little more. It's important to note that the inner line of the seam allowance must be turned. ## Final Touches Finally, manually drag the board to make the fold distribution a little more even. Don't forget to reduce the diameter of the inner board to 10 and the thickness to 1. ### Conclusion We have reached the end of this tutorial. The waistband and the waistband are almost the same. If we see that one side is not very even, the reason may be that we didn't use the "TURN" line type here. So, we use the edge sewing line tool to change the sewing line type of this side to "TURN." It will result in a much more even appearance. Finally, we can reduce the particle diameter to 5 so that the folds are more detailed. Thank you so much for watching! I hope you enjoyed this video. Don't forget to click the like button; this helps me to complete the steps for the next video. See you next time! ```
